newsitem.title: ITALY: Gemina sees 1996 cons net at 210 bln lire.
newsitem.headline: Gemina sees 1996 cons net at 210 bln lire.

text.p: Italian financial holding company Gemina SpA said it estimated 1996 consolidated net profit of 210 billion lire ($123.6 million) which it described as a "decisive turning point" and the best result in the company's history.
Gemina posted a net consolidated loss for 1995 of 678.5 billion lire.
In a statement after a board meeting to examine preliminary 1996 figures, Gemina said its parent company's 1996 net profit was estimated at over 90 billion lire after a loss of 186 billion in 1995.

Gemina said the inversion of trend derived from an improvement in consolidated results of its industrial units which had overall turnover of 6.018 trillion lire in 1996 against 5.654 billion in 1995, with net profit of 230 billion against a 611 billion loss in 1995.
In particular, Gemina mentioned its RCS Editori publishing unit which returned to the black with a consolidated profit of around one billion lire after a 1995 loss of 729 billion.
Its Fila sportswear company exceeded good growth rates in past years with a record 1996 consolidated net profit of 178 billion lire.
The GFT textiles company posted a consolidated net profit of 51 billion lire against 18 billion in 1995 setting a record result.
Gemina said its net consolidated financial position at end 1996 showed liquidity equal to 1.152 trillion lire.
The parent company result would allow the company to pay a savings share dividend for 1996 as well as for 1995 and 1994.

Gemina said the spin-off of its industrial activities into Holding di Partecipazioni Industriali SpA (HPI) which it announced late last year had now been completed and took effect from Thursday March 6.
HPI will be quoted on the Milan bourse from March 10.
